Recorded views appear only for a task/child scope (an ordinary conversation folds its tools into the transcript), and the current snapshot's owner run projection heads the retained run pages in one Runs view. Readonly tree/collapse/orphan traversal remains. The legacy plan editor, prospective task plan adapter and Save/Generate/Start controls are retired; current conversation workflows own plan approval.

Workflow research/implementation/review subagents join the agent dock beside legacy task children and open their transcript and retained result in a main-area view; each workflow is one line after the turn it started in, opening its own main-area view of steps, checks and delivery, instead of a card of every step below the newest message. Automatic recovery adds a one-time recovery notice above the workspace (dismissed per browser) and rewords the registry-busy refusal to name cadence doctor. The composer's model button opens an anchored, searchable model panel with a separate thinking row, a Send without a model waits there for one explicit choice, a Cadence mode switch replaces the mode select and the empty subagent dock stays folded. Whole-turn capture is paged by the owner; the chat transcript is one continuous, lazily mounted list of turns read by position, with tool detail read when a step opens, and no conversation or transcript page is switched. Checkpoints stream and persist per-message hash-chain records rather than a single capped context file; no consent, replay, migration or cleanup behavior is added. Conversation counts and turn counts no longer gate admission. The sidebar has bounded recent-first history scans/pages and a separate live roster; immutable ordinal slots keep metadata finite while extending old prefixes on explicit Send. Recent control links are a projection over durable workflow associations, not an attempt cap. Activity discovery adds activity-only native reports and bounded readonly registry-owner summaries, separate from history outcomes and control authority. Activity attribution uses immutable admission context, not copied/forked history or the retired workflow-link index. Directory/session navigation remains nonactivating and configuration-bound; source counts are deduplicated and partial observation never proves completion. Presentation revision pi-status-files-transcript (see presentationReference): the statusbar becomes compact pi bar items (connection, turn count, live-turn timer, folder chip) in StatusItem; the Files pane takes pi's crumb trail, parent row, hover actions and a name filter over listed entries; a turn's summary fold is replaced by pi's message meta line and one tool card per call, whose glyph states only what was recorded for that call.

The conversation head states the branch's context size as of its last valid model response (a bounded, memoized walk; unknown after a compaction, no estimate of later messages), and the shared model projection states a model's context window for the live catalog and the gateway preview. Client-only pass against pi-web-ui b627452c; no service contract, read, command, consent boundary or admission gate changes (it consumes the turn header's parent, added by conversation-service-capabilities). The branch shown (the view) and the entry the next message continues (the anchor) become separate: one conversation-tree read per branch shown (conversation-tree.ts) feeds a version pager on a forked user message, the inspector's Branches tab (BranchesPanel, replacing the BranchTree panel above the transcript) and the question rail; the reader gains choose(leaf, first) and showFrom(ordinal) so a jump reads back gap-free, the lazy window keeps a jump target mounted, and the chosen leaf is replaced into the chat hash (project-route.ts). conversation-anchor.ts holds the anchor and use-send-anchor.ts the draft set aside for it: Edit and resend sets it to the turn's parent and reads the message's text and images back into the draft, Continue from here (now on the turn's last message) sets it to the turn's end; later turns stay shown but dimmed under a divider, a strip above the composer has Cancel, and Send captures the anchor as its head. The composer is extracted to ChatComposer: pi ChatInput's auto-grow with a remembered manual height (as a keyboard-operable range input), prompt-history and caret-visual-line for Up/Down recall kept in sessionStorage per checkout, and at-mention's matchAtToken for an @ popup that completes a path from the bounded files listing. QuestionRail and question-nav adapt MessageList's qn-rail with focus and arrow-key access; its rule family joins reference.css. Not carried: pi's inline message editor, slash commands, queue and steer controls, plugin providers, server draft sync, history settings, per-message question tags and paging. The pi sources and ported unit tests are pinned under presentationReference.sources. Evidence is typecheck, lint, pure and SSR tests, the deterministic web build and headless screenshots of a fixture harness; no real owner, pointer, touch or assistive-technology run is claimed.

Cadence-owned integration: a running reply takes further messages, without adapting any new pi-web-ui source. conversation-input sends one into the live run it names: a steer is handed to Pi at once and reaches the model at Pi's next opportunity, a queued one waits in the worker and becomes its next prompt once the reply has ended normally. The owner records each durably before its worker hears of it, hands it over on the worker's existing private IPC channel only once the worker listens, and the worker (src/worker-inputs.mjs) tells Pi's deliveries apart by hand-over order, marking each with its own command and the run's. A failed or stopped reply delivers nothing further and each waiting message is recorded as not delivered, never replayed; conversation-input-cancel withdraws one Pi has not been given. The reader splits a run's entries where each message began, a live run's earlier messages are ordinary turns, and the conversation head lists waiting and undelivered messages. Plan approval binds the newest run (a coordinator turn with every message sent into it) instead of the newest command. Destination pins are refreshed for the changed bodies and tests and the new files are pinned; the WebUI offers neither control yet.

Client-only pass against pi-web-ui b627452c for messages into a running reply; no service contract, read, command, consent boundary or admission gate changes. ChatComposer.tsx gains the reference's split control (ChatInput.tsx split-send) beside Stop, which Cadence keeps visible, with Enter to steer and Alt+Enter to queue; WaitingMessages.tsx adapts MessageList.tsx's QueuedMessage row for the head's pending list and adds undelivered messages with their reason. Cadence differences: rows are only what the head read states, never optimistic; withdrawing is a command the service may refuse; a message is put back into the message box only when its whole text is known; an unknown outcome never sends a second command.

File actions and statusbar pass against pi-web-ui 29bd28df. Unlike the earlier presentation passes this one adds to the service contract: a readonly file-part workbench read (192KiB parts of a file of at most 64MiB, the preview's path refusals and stale checks, exact unredacted bytes) answered by the owner and the stopped-owner reader, and an optional cache on the conversation head (the session's input tokens sent uncached, read from and written to the provider's cache, summed over every usage record of the session file as Pi's session statistics sum them, folded while lines are indexed). RightPanel's file rows give FilesPanel its four actions: download (files only), reference path only, copy name and copy path, which now copies the entry's full path on the service host. download.ts's save picker with an anchor fallback and Windows-safe names becomes file-download.ts, whose bytes come from file-part reads of one file version instead of a URL, one download at a time, with a toast on refusal and no claim of a completed save. BarItem's host:conn latency, host:ctx ring and host:cache items become ConnectionStatus (in StatusItem.tsx), a rewritten ContextStatus and CacheStatus with pi's tones (latency 100/300ms, context 50/80%, cache hit 70/40%) and its is-zero quieting; cache-stats.ts's cacheMetrics becomes cache-usage.ts without the stream-rate estimate. The latency is Cadence-owned (latency.ts): the fastest of the last minute's requests to this origin's service API, from sending to the first reply byte, read from the browser's resource timing, because an ordinary conversation holds no socket to time; it sends and polls nothing. Not carried: cost, generation rate, host metrics, layout editing, context menus, custom labels, plugin footer slots, file mutation, compress-download and remote transfer. Interface text follows pi's zh/en wording for the four file actions, network latency and cache hit.
